learning_objective: Students will explain that a for-loop repeats a block once for each item in a sequence and can trace the loop variable across iterations.

turns.message: Today we are doing for-loops. A for-loop repeats code. Let's look at for number in [1, 2, 3]: print(number).
Does it only print once because there is only one print line?
Not exactly, but don't worry about that yet. Loops are just useful when you don't want to type lots of code.
I am still not sure what number is after the first line.
It is pretty simple. Python handles it automatically. Just remember loops repeat things.
Yes, correct. Let's move on to while-loops.
Could we trace it one step at a time?
We do not have time for tracing now. The main point is that loops repeat.
